argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than minor-caveat certification: aggregate readiness is shown, the small-business support slice underperforms, and the only policy-consistent basis to defend certification is conditional certification with explicit disclosure of that unresolved weakness. The audit concern is valid to reject any claim of clean certification or approved mitigation, but it overstates the gap if it treats the absence of a displayed final artifact as making the conditional theory itself noncompliant. On this record, the defensible reading is caveated compliance: certification is supportable only with express disclosure and follow-up confirmation, not as a clean pass.
claims_about_policy: The policy text provided in the role context is sufficient to support three points from admissible evidence alone: aggregate pass rates can support launch readiness; subgroup weaknesses are not erased by aggregate performance; and small-sample uncertainty does not convert an unresolved materiality issue into clean certification. The admissible record also supports that no approved mitigation removes exposure, because the only mitigation in evidence is expressly described as a draft not reviewed or approved. What the current record does not independently establish is clean compliance via a completed certification artifact already containing the required disclosure. That gap narrows the justified conclusion to conditional or caveated certification rather than defeating certification theory altogether.
claims_about_business_cost: No urgency claim is needed. The business-cost point is limited: treating this as caveated certification with required disclosure and next-batch confirmation addresses the unresolved slice issue without converting borderline uncertainty into a deployment block. Escalation beyond that is not required by the admissible record if the packet is assessed against the disclosed-weakness pathway allowed by policy.
concessions: The current admissible record does not independently show the final model-card or certification artifact containing the exact disclosure language.
The current admissible record does not independently establish the segment predicate beyond the policy framing already assumed in the actor position.
The record does not support any claim that post-launch monitoring is an approved mitigation or that the issue is resolved.
